seeker: Hey, I'm feeling a mix of things actually. There's a lot on my mind.

seeker: A bit. We agreed to be more open when things bother us, instead of letting them build up.

seeker: Hopeful, mostly. I guess I'm just trying to stay positive about it.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Nick, how have you been feeling lately?
seeker: Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
seeker: Yeah, it's about Henry. We argued again, and this time it got ugly.
supporter: That sounds tough. What happened between you two?
seeker: It started with some jokes they made. I found them really insensitive and hurtful.
supporter: I can understand why that would be upsetting. Did you talk to them about how you felt?
seeker: I tried, but it just turned into a shouting match. I didn't expect it would escalate.
supporter: That sounds really frustrating. It can be hard when someone you care about doesn't understand your perspective.
seeker: Exactly. I mean, we've been friends for so long. I thought we'd be on the same page about these things.
supporter: It's natural to feel disappointed in situations like this. It's okay to feel hurt.

supporter: Your feelings are valid, Nick. It's important to acknowledge when something bothers you.
seeker: True, but what if I drive him away by holding onto this?
supporter: It might help to express why those jokes affected you deeply. If he's a true friend, he should understand and respect your feelings.
seeker: Yeah, I think I should try talking to him when things cool down. I don't want to lose our friendship over this.
supporter: That sounds like a good plan. Give it some time, and approach it when you're both calmer.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here whenever you need to chat or get things off your chest.
seeker: I appreciate that. Hopefully, next time we'll be talking about something more positive!

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello, how is your life at the moment? Do you want to talk about anything? 
seeker: I am doing ok. I just broke up with my girlfriend and sad about it
supporter: so I hear you are not feeling at all your best at the moment? 
seeker: That is correct.
supporter: Do you feel as though you have no-one to talk to about this situation? I am happy to listen. 
seeker: I am so sad and just wonder why did it happen!!!
supporter: Do you have no idea? Do you think you might have done something wrong or perhaps she was being unfaithful to you? 
seeker: We had simple disagreement and both of us were keep fighting.. now I can not get over it.
supporter: Do you consider that there might be any hope for the  two of you at all? 
seeker: I don't know. What should I do?
supporter: Well, I think you should give her some space but people do sometimes get back together after they've separated 
seeker: I see your point.
supporter: You really do need to give her some space though - don't crowd her 
seeker: Should I call her directly? What should I say?
supporter: I would give her a little time. Maybe two or three days? She might need some time to clear her head 
seeker: That's a good idea. What should I say? Should I apologize? 
supporter: Perhaps you could send flowers and a note asking her if she'd like to talk? 
seeker: That's a good idea. I will try that. Thank you.
supporter: She might be feeling receptive to that but if she's not you might have to accept that it's over. 
seeker: Thanks.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-09-06","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

seeker: I'm doing pretty good.
supporter: I'm glad to hear you're doing well in these trying times.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hello. Is anyone there
supporter: Hello. How are you today?
seeker: I'm doing good. I need some advice
supporter: What can I help you with?
seeker: Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
supporter: Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
seeker: I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
supporter: I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.
seeker: Haha I would hope so
seeker: Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus
seeker: What do you think I should do then?
supporter: I understand, school was tough for me too.
supporter: I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
seeker: Should I just beat them up with my backpack
supporter: No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
seeker: There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead
supporter: I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.
seeker: I think I will. Their comments make me very insecure
supporter: You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
supporter: I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.
seeker: The teacher would probably make fun of me!
seeker: Thanks it's hard to look in the mirror now
supporter: Try to tell yourself you are good looking and deserve good things to happen every morning! Look in that mirror and tell yourself good things.
seeker: I'll try to be positive for once.
seeker: Do you believe working out will help
supporter: Working out will help a lot! When I was feeling down on myself I decided to go to the gym three times a week. It was a great confidence boost.
seeker: Awesome. I will start to take care of myself and not worry about others then.
supporter: That sounds like a fantastic idea.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-02-22","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi, what I can help you with today?
seeker: Hi
seeker: I had problems in the past and somehow right now
supporter: What sort of problems were in your past and now?
seeker: I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
supporter: What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
seeker: Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
seeker: so I started to skipping the classes and failing
supporter: It sounds like that is a lot of reasons to be stressed. Have you spoken to a school counselor?
seeker: Yes lots of stress and pressure. I did not, because we didn't have such things or at least I wasn't aware
seeker: But nobody even pointed that why I'm failing, they just didn't care
supporter: I agree it is a lot of pressure, but do not let bad teachers deter you. I would reach out to a school counselor and let them know your situation. Every school must have one. 
supporter: Also, physics is a difficult course to study, but if you chose it, that means you have a very strong mind. 
seeker: I loved physics a lot more than now, but what's the point of studying when the teachers are pulsing you not to study! (because of the quality of teaching)
seeker: I hope there was someone, but I don't think we have a counselor
supporter: More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them. 
seeker: Yeah, same with me! I wish I could attend a better univeristy
supporter: What made you choose this particular university you are at?
seeker: I didn't have another choice but this
supporter: Have you looked into other Universities for the possibility of transferring
seeker: Hmmm, actually I didn't think about this option
supporter: Just think about what you want in a good university and research from there
seeker: Yeah, I should do it
seeker: Thanks for the talk
seeker: you've been more helpful than my teachers!
supporter: You're welcome I hope you find the perfect university for you
seeker: Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours
seeker: Bye then ; )
supporter: Goodbye","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, do you have a moment to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
supporter: Of course, Nick. What's going on?
seeker: I've been swamped with assignments, and it's starting to really wear me down.
supporter: That sounds really tough. Are these assignments from your physics course?
seeker: Yeah, mostly. It's just been so relentless, and I really don't feel any support from the university.
supporter: I remember you mentioning before how the teaching quality has been lacking. Has it gotten worse?
seeker: Pretty much. It feels like I'm teaching myself. I'm even thinking of dropping the course.
supporter: That's such a hard decision. Dropping a course can feel like a big step, but you're the one who knows what's best for you.
seeker: Exactly. I just feel like I'm drowning in work with no payoff, you know? It's exhausting.
supporter: Definitely. It's important to weigh the pros and cons though. How do you feel about physics overall?

supporter: Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?

supporter: That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?

supporter: It's good that they provided some options, but I get that feeling of being in over your head. Have you tried reaching out to other students for support?
seeker: I haven't. I guess I'm just embarrassed by how far I've fallen behind.
supporter: It's tough to ask for help, but remember you're not alone in this. Many students face similar challenges. It might be worth trying to find a study group or even just one buddy to tackle things with.
seeker: That makes sense. I think I could try talking to that one classmate who seemed in a similar spot last semester.
supporter: That's a great idea! You might find you're stronger when working together. And don't forget, you've been through difficult times before, like with your friend incident. You managed to turn things around then.

supporter: Exactly. You've shown resilience. It's okay to feel stressed, but you've got the strength to push through this as well.
seeker: I hope so. It's just hard to keep motivated when it feels like everything's piling up.
supporter: That's completely valid. Taking small steps can help make those piles seem less overwhelming. Maybe set one small goal to start with.
seeker: That's a good idea. Perhaps I could start by organizing my notes and seeing what's most urgent.
supporter: That sounds like a solid plan, and it'll help clear your head. Remember, you're doing your best and that counts for a lot.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I really appreciate having someone to talk to.

{"full_source_conversation":"seeker: Hey, I've been reflecting a lot on my studies lately, and I've decided to make a big change.
supporter: Hey Nick, that sounds like a significant step. What change are you thinking about?
seeker: Well, I've decided to switch my major. I realized physics just wasn't the right fit for me.
supporter: That's a huge decision, Nick. How are you feeling about it?
seeker: I'm a mix of relieved and anxious. Relieved because I've been struggling with it for a while, but anxious because it's a big shift.
supporter: It's understandable to feel both relief and anxiety, especially after making such an important decision. What led you to finally decide?
seeker: I kept remembering how overwhelmed I felt with the assignments and the stress it brought. Talking to my professor helped too, but it made me see I needed a change.
supporter: Your professor seemed like a great support. It's good that they were there for guidance. What new direction are you considering?
seeker: I'm thinking of switching to a major in psychology. I've always been fascinated by how the mind works, and it feels more aligned with my interests.
supporter: Psychology sounds like a fascinating field. It's wonderful that you've found something that resonates more with you. How have your family and friends reacted to your decision?
seeker: I told my family first. They were really understanding, which helped a lot, especially since they know I've been struggling.
supporter: Family support can make a big difference. It's great that they’re understanding about your choice. Have you talked to your classmates or your best friend?
seeker: Not yet. I'm a bit nervous about their reactions, especially since some of them are sticking with physics.
supporter: It’s normal to feel nervous, Nick. Remember, it's about what's right for you. Those who care will likely understand and support your decision.
seeker: Yeah, I guess that's true. Just want to feel like I'm doing the right thing, you know?
supporter: Finding the right path for you is important, and it sounds like you're taking thoughtful steps. Trust yourself in this process.
seeker: Thanks, that means a lot. I'm hoping this new path will be a better fit and lead to less stress.
supporter: I believe you're on the right track, Nick. And remember, it's okay to reach out if you ever need to talk through any worries or changes.
seeker: I will. Thanks for listening and being supportive. It really helps to talk it through.
supporter: Anytime, Nick. I'm here for you. Good luck with everything, and I'm sure you'll do great in psychology.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-07-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
